narrative.overview:
The whole guide is one transit diagram. Every track is a coloured line, every lesson is a stop, and the learner can always see where they are. Surfaces are quiet and dark-first; the colour is carried by the lines, not by the chrome. Signage is the reference material: condensed station-board headings, square plates, thick-ringed stops, a single five-colour stripe.

Density is calm and reading-led. Lesson prose sits in a 44rem measure beside short code chunks and their real captured output. The seven themes are fixed palettes the learner chooses between; the Metro world is layered on top of whichever is active and never replaces it.
keyCharacteristics: Five line colours derived per theme from that theme's own accent.
Condensed sign face for headings and labels, humanist sans for reading, mono for code only.
Square sign plates: radius scale capped at 8px, 3-4px typical.
One primary action per page, the plate.
One signature: the 4px five-colour stripe under the top bar.
Seven themes, each with its own quiet background texture (switchable off).

rules.name: The Derived Line Rule
rules.body: Line colours are always computed from the active theme's accent. Never introduce a sixth colour or a hand-picked line palette for a new theme; set --color-accent and the lines follow.

rules.name: The Plate Is The Only Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Accent fill appears on one plate per view. Lines and stops carry colour elsewhere.

rules.name: The Sign Face Rule
rules.body: Condensed type is for names of things (stops, lines, plates), never for paragraphs.

rules.name: The No Ligatures Rule
rules.body: Mono text renders exact characters; ligatures and contextual alternates are disabled everywhere.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Plates, stops and cards never take drop shadows of their own. Depth is a tint and a border.

dos: Do set a new theme's colours and only --color-accent for lines; let --line-1..5 derive.
Do keep every radius at 8px or below; plates 3px, panels 4px.
Do use one plate per page for the primary action.
Do draw progress as stops: filled when done, ringed when next.
Do keep mono for code and output; headings in the sign face.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion; the only ambient motion is the next-stop pulse and a 0.4s fade-up on entry.
donts: Don't add a card grid, centred hero or feature columns as the page frame.
Don't hard-code line or accent colours in components; read the variables.
Don't use ink-faint for anything a learner must read to act.
Don't make themes share a single background texture; each theme draws its own and the Background setting must switch it off.
Don't use rounded pills or soft large radii for controls.
